name: cross_scale_systems
title: Systems across scales
description: A grid of four study systems against three scales: within individuals, between individuals and across populations. Solid outlines mark a published paper at that scale; dashed outlines mark collaborative or unpublished work. Foot-and-mouth disease virus in African buffalo has published work on virus growth and immune response and on transmission between buffalo including carrier infection, and a collaborative cells-to-landscapes project in which the author develops within-host models. Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus in livestock and wildlife has collaborative work on antibody response in livestock and on transmission between livestock and wildlife hosts. Human cultural transmission has published work on networks and clusters of cultural traits and on cultural variation across geography and language. Bighorn sheep immune ecology has collaborative work on immune phenotypes of individual sheep and immune variation among metapopulations. A chain below states that ecological and landscape change influences movement and contact, which shapes connectivity among populations and so persistence, divergence and evolution.

name: software_stack
title: Simulation, inference and decisions
description: Public tools cover field/equation/reaction specification with OP System, PDE/nonlocal/reaction simulation with OP Engine, campaigns with FlepiMoP2, and replicated evaluation with trade-study. op_infer adds selected inference adapters, calibration and study-design checks as research software in development.

name: obs_model_general
title: Models and measurements across scientific domains
description: An underlying process x(t) is linked to recorded data y through an observation model p(y given x and measurement parameters). Established examples cover health, ecology and incomplete multivariate data; monitoring design is marked as a developing direction that requires domain collaboration.

name: future_directions_general
title: Current research directions
description: Three connected, nonsequential areas distinguish established applications, methods and software, and developing questions in scientific machine learning, monitoring, surveillance and study design.

name: op_system_slide
title: OP System compilation and numerical interfaces
description: A model specification feeds a compiler, which exports evaluators, operator/reaction metadata, and observation/forcing interfaces. Model classes include PDEs, nonlocal dynamics, compartments and reactions. Numerical consumers choose discretization and integration; cross-axis constraints remain metadata.

name: op_engine_slide
title: OP Engine method families
description: A capability table groups deterministic solvers, stochastic solvers and schedule replay. It lists PDE/field, nonlocal, ODE and reaction models, observations and optional firing counts. Independent SSA clocks use NumPy. Replay derivatives are conditional on the recorded mesh; tested backends vary by method.

name: op_infer_slide
title: op_infer research capabilities
description: op_infer capabilities include selected inference-library adapters, calibration checks on simulated data, and replicated study comparisons. The source is public research software in development.

name: flepimop2_slide
title: FlepiMoP2 provider relationships
description: Validated configuration selects campaign targets connected to System/Parameter, Engine, Backend, Process and Job providers. Connections indicate interface relationships, not execution order. Cores can also run independently.

name: trade_study_slide
title: Replicated design and evaluation with trade-study
description: Candidate designs feed replicated simulator/scorer evaluations and trial results. Results branch into comparisons and optional analyses, with a dashed return for adaptive search or phase refinement. Calibration and transfer require separate application evidence.

name: pp_eigentest_schematic
title: Signal rank with incomplete data
description: Ongoing signal-rank research connects incomplete data, Bayesian latent-variable modeling, and assessment of signal and uncertainty. The methods and software remain in development.

name: vbpca_py_schematic
title: VBPCApy observed-data model
description: An illustrative masked data matrix feeds a variational low-rank model for latent scores, loadings, bias, noise and ARD priors. Model outputs branch to fitted-data reconstruction, training scores and assessment. Covariances are approximate; coverage and rank recovery need checks for the intended data.

name: optimal_design
title: Illustrative observation-design tradeoffs
description: Synthetic candidate costs and utilities illustrate Pareto efficiency and selection under a declared budget. These values are illustrative inputs, not a fitted study or empirical information estimates.

name: structural_fidelity_comparison
title: Illustrative constraint checks for predictions
description: Two constructed prevalence curves compared with an upper bound of one over the displayed horizon. One stays below the bound and the other crosses it; predictive accuracy is not evaluated.

name: npzd_hysteresis
title: Forward hysteresis in an NPZD model
description: Two panels from the rescaled nutrient-phytoplankton-zooplankton-detritus (NPZD) model of Macdonald and Gulbudak (2023), recomputed from its equations with parameters from the paper. Panel a: equilibrium phytoplankton against the maximum harmful effect of phytoplankton on zooplankton. Above the threshold at which the paper's zooplankton persistence number equals one, the zooplankton-free equilibrium is locally stable and no coexistence equilibrium exists. Below it a coexistence branch bifurcates forward and folds twice, giving two stable coexistence states with an unstable state between them over an intermediate range. Stable branches are solid; unstable branches are dashed or dotted. Panel b: two simulations at a marked value in that range, differing only in initial zooplankton, settle on different stable states: low initial zooplankton on the high-phytoplankton state and high initial zooplankton on the low-phytoplankton state. Not copied from the paper.

name: rk4_known_solution
title: Truncation and round-off against a known solution
description: Panel a: logistic growth with its closed-form solution, with eight fixed steps of fourth-order Runge-Kutta marked. Panel b: absolute error at the final time against the number of steps, in float64 and float32. Error falls as the fourth power of the step until round-off dominates; float32 reaches its floor near one part in ten million after about forty steps and the error then grows with the step count, while float64 reaches its floor near one part in ten to the fifteenth. One method on one problem with a known solution; errors of exactly zero are drawn at the axis floor.

name: siwr_reservoir_speed
title: One reproduction number, two transmission routes
description: New infections per day per thousand hosts in a susceptible-infectious-reservoir model with basic reproduction number 2.5 and a five-day infectious period, for three splits of transmission between direct contact and a shared environmental reservoir. Panel a: a slowly decaying reservoir (decay 0.05 per day) gives three distinct curves, later and lower as the reservoir share rises. Panel b: a fast reservoir (decay 5 per day) gives curves that coincide, so case counts alone cannot separate the routes. Assumed parameters; no inference is performed.

name: record_type_precision
title: Growth-rate precision from two kinds of record
description: Panel a: one simulated epidemic growing at 0.08 per day from fifty infections per day, recorded as an environmental signal sampled every two days with log-normal noise and as daily reported counts with one percent reporting. Panel b: standard error of the estimated growth rate against days of data, for the environmental signal in closed form (checked by 800 simulations) and for Poisson counts at ten, one and one tenth of a percent reporting. Which record is more precise depends on the reporting fraction and the length of the record. Assumed values; detection time is not compared.
